global_conventions.auth: Handled entirely by the platform. All tools execute inside an already-authenticated customer session; no auth token is passed between tools. Every write tool still requires explicit customer confirmation in conversation before it is called.
global_conventions.session_context: login_context (customer_id, full_name, date_of_birth, gender, customer_since, customer_segment, registered_mobile, registered_email, communication_address, permanent_address, kyc_status, pan_masked, preferred_language, linked_products_summary, linked_accounts, linked_products, linked_cards) is injected into the system prompt at session start. linked_products entries carry their product type (fd, rd, loan, policy). linked_products_summary is a quick-glance count by type only — full IDs still come from linked_products. date_of_birth and customer_segment (enum: regular | premium | wealth | senior_citizen | staff) are the eligibility signals for senior_citizen_rate in get_deposit_loan_rates and for personalised offers in get_products_and_offers. kyc_status (enum: verified | pending | expired) may cause write tools to fail — check the returned message field in that case. communication_address/permanent_address reflect the last verified update, not any pending address-update request submitted via raise_request. registered_mobile, registered_email, and pan_masked are masked, display-only values. All IDs passed to tools must come from login_context or from a prior tool result — never invented or assumed.
global_conventions.naming: Array inputs use plural names (e.g. account_ids). All IDs are opaque tokens, never raw PANs or card numbers.
global_conventions.write_outcomes: Every write tool returns status (success|failed) and message (human-readable outcome or failure reason). Tools that act directly on an account, card or deposit also return reference_id (audit reference). Tools that create a trackable service request — raise_request, request_cheque_book, request_duplicate_statement — return request_id instead; that IS their audit reference, and they do not return reference_id.
global_conventions.dates: YYYY-MM-DD for dates, ISO 8601 for timestamps.
global_conventions.amounts: Always positive numbers. Direction (credit/debit) is carried by a separate 'type' field, never by the sign of the amount. All amounts are in INR (Indian Rupees) unless otherwise stated.
global_conventions.confirmation_policy: action_type='write' tools require explicit customer confirmation in the conversation before being called, regardless of whether prerequisites were already satisfied.

function.name: search_knowledge_base
function.description:
Searches the bank's knowledge corpus (product documents, RBI circulars, scheme details, FAQs, how-to guides) with a natural-language query. Use for policy, process, eligibility, or regulatory questions that cannot be answered from the customer's own account or product data.

Category: knowledge | Action type: read

Notes:
- Any rule or policy quoted in a response to the customer must be grounded in the snippets returned by this tool — never asserted from memory.

query.description: Natural-language question or search phrase. Example: 'premature FD penalty rules'.

function.name: get_account_balance
function.description:
Returns current available balance and hold/lien amount for one or more linked accounts.

Category: accounts | Action type: read

function.name: get_account_details
function.description:
Returns account metadata — type, status, home branch, IFSC, holders, nominee, open date. Does not return balances (use get_account_balance) or transactions (use get_transaction_history).

Category: accounts | Action type: read

function.name: get_transaction_history
function.description:
Returns statement entries for a single account, newest first, with date/direction/channel filters and pagination.

Category: accounts | Action type: read

Notes:
- Each returned entry includes a status field (e.g. success, pending, failed, reversed) reflecting the transaction's processing state. This status is specific to this tool's output — it is not carried into the official statement produced by request_duplicate_statement.

from_date.description: Start of date range. No lower bound if omitted.

to_date.description: End of date range. No upper bound if omitted.

function.name: get_fd_details
function.description:
Returns full details of the customer's Fixed Deposits.

Category: deposits | Action type: read

Related tools: get_rd_details, update_deposit_renewal, get_deposit_closure_quote, close_deposit

Notes:
- Mandatory prerequisite before update_deposit_renewal and get_deposit_closure_quote — always surface the current state before proposing a change or showing a closure quote.
- payout_account defaults to source_account at the time of booking and cannot be changed on an active deposit. The only way to redirect proceeds is the optional payout_account override at close_deposit time.

function.name: get_rd_details
function.description:
Returns full details of the customer's Recurring Deposits, including installment amount, installments paid so far, and total accumulated to date.

Category: deposits | Action type: read

Related tools: get_fd_details, update_deposit_renewal, get_deposit_closure_quote, close_deposit

Notes:
- Mandatory prerequisite before update_deposit_renewal and get_deposit_closure_quote — always surface the current state before proposing a change or showing a closure quote.
- total_deposited is the accumulated-so-far figure; maturity_amount is the projected final figure. Do not conflate the two when answering the customer.
- payout_account defaults to source_account at the time of booking and cannot be changed on an active deposit. The only way to redirect proceeds is the optional payout_account override at close_deposit time.

function.name: get_deposit_loan_rates
function.description:
Returns the current rate card for a deposit or loan product, by tenure/amount slab. The sole authoritative source for any rate used in a calculator or a booking — never use memory, assumption, or a customer-supplied rate.

Category: rates | Action type: read

Related tools: calculate_fd_maturity, calculate_rd_maturity, calculate_emi, create_fd, create_rd

tenure_months.description: Filter to the slab covering this tenure. All slabs if omitted.

amount.description: Filter to the slab covering this amount. All slabs if omitted.

function.name: calculate_fd_maturity
function.description:
Computes maturity value and interest earned for a Fixed Deposit. Compounding is quarterly by default (bank standard) and not configurable via input.

Category: calculators | Action type: calculator

Call before this tool, in order:
?. get_deposit_loan_rates — rate must be sourced here, never assumed or taken from the customer

Related tools: create_fd, get_deposit_loan_rates

Notes:
- For payout_type of monthly or quarterly, the maturity_amount returned is principal only — interest is paid out periodically during the tenure rather than accumulated to maturity.

function.name: calculate_rd_maturity
function.description:
Computes maturity value and interest earned for a Recurring Deposit. Interest is always paid at maturity. Compounding is quarterly by default (bank standard) and not configurable via input.

Category: calculators | Action type: calculator

Call before this tool, in order:
?. get_deposit_loan_rates — rate must be sourced here, never assumed or taken from the customer

Related tools: create_rd, get_deposit_loan_rates

Notes:
- Mandatory prerequisite before create_rd.
- RDs have no periodic payout option — interest always accrues and is credited only at maturity, unlike FDs which support monthly/quarterly payout.

tenure_months.description: Tenure in months (= number of installments).

function.name: create_fd
function.description:
Books a new Fixed Deposit, debiting principal_amount from the source account as a one-time transaction.

Category: deposits | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Call before this tool, in order:
1. get_deposit_loan_rates — obtain the applicable rate based on the user's age
2. calculate_fd_maturity — show the customer the rate and projected maturity value before booking
3. get_account_balance — verify the source account can fund principal_amount

Notes:
- payout_account is not a separate input — proceeds to source_account and cannot be changed later on an active deposit.
- If payout_type is non-cumulative (monthly or quarterly), maturity_instruction cannot be renew_principal_interest — interest is already being paid out periodically, so there is no accumulated interest left to renew. Only no_renewal or renew_principal are valid in that case.

source_account.description: Linked account to debit once, at booking.

guardian_name.description: Required if nominee's date_of_birth indicates the nominee is under 18 at the time of registration. Must be validated at call time even though not schema-enforced.

function.name: create_rd
function.description:
Books a new Recurring Deposit. This authorizes a recurring monthly debit of monthly_installment from source_account for the entire tenure; the first installment is debited at booking. This recurring commitment must be stated explicitly when seeking customer confirmation.

Category: deposits | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Call before this tool, in order:
1. get_deposit_loan_rates — obtain the applicable rate
2. calculate_rd_maturity — show the customer the rate and projected maturity value before booking
3. get_account_balance — verify the source account can fund the first installment — note this does NOT verify the customer can sustain the full multi-month commitment; confirm that separately in conversation

Notes:
- payout_account is not a separate input — proceeds default to source_account and cannot be changed later on an active deposit.
- No payout_type input — RDs always pay interest at maturity only.
- maturity_instruction is optional and defaults to no_renewal. It can only be set here, at booking: update_deposit_renewal is FD-only, so an RD's maturity instruction cannot be changed once the RD is active.

tenure_months.description: Tenure in months (= number of installments).

source_account.description: Linked account debited monthly for the full tenure.

guardian_name.description: Required if nominee's date_of_birth indicates the nominee is under 18 at the time of registration. Must be validated at call time even though not schema-enforced.

function.name: get_deposit_closure_quote
function.description:
Quotes the payout if an FD or RD were closed today. Before maturity, interest is credited only at the card rate applicable to the period the deposit has actually run — normally lower than the rate contracted for its original tenure — and a separate premature-closure charge of penalty_rate% of principal_amount is then deducted. After maturity no charge applies (penalty_rate = 0) and the full contracted interest is paid. estimated_payout is the net figure after any charge; effective_rate is the net annual rate the customer actually earns. Read-only — does not close anything.

Category: deposits | Action type: read

Call before this tool, in order:
0. get_fd_details — surface the current FD state before showing the closure quote
0. get_rd_details — surface the current RD state before showing the closure quote

Related tools: close_deposit, get_fd_details, get_rd_details

Notes:
- Mandatory prerequisite before close_deposit — the quote, including any penalty, must be shown to the customer before they confirm closure.
- When penalty_rate is 0 (post-maturity closure), penalty_amount will also be 0.
- principal_amount (number) is returned for both FD and RD quotes: for an FD it is the original principal (see get_fd_details.principal_amount); for an RD it is the sum of installments paid to date.

function.name: close_deposit
function.description:
Closes an FD or RD prematurely and credits proceeds to the payout account. For an RD, closure also permanently stops all future monthly installment debits — there is no separate way to 'pause' or 'stop' an RD without closing it.

Category: deposits | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Call before this tool, in order:
1. get_deposit_closure_quote — show the customer the payout amount and any penalty before they confirm closure

function.name: update_deposit_renewal
function.description:
Sets the maturity instruction on an active FD. Takes effect on the maturity date, not immediately.

Category: deposits | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Call before this tool, in order:
1. get_fd_details — surface the current instruction and maturity date before changing it

Notes:
- If the deposit's payout_type (from get_fd_details) is non-cumulative (monthly or quarterly), instruction cannot be set to renew_principal_interest — only no_renewal or renew_principal are valid.

function.name: get_loan_details
function.description:
Returns current loan state: outstanding balance, EMI, rate, remaining tenure, next due date.

Category: loans | Action type: read

Related tools: get_loan_foreclosure_quote, calculate_emi

function.name: get_loan_foreclosure_quote
function.description:
Quotes the total payoff to close a loan early as of a given date. Informational only — no tool in this system closes a loan.

Category: loans | Action type: read

Related tools: get_loan_details

Notes:
- If a customer asks to 'pause', 'stop', or 'reduce' EMIs, use this tool to show foreclosure cost, since no such capability exists in this system.
- No tool in this system closes a loan. After presenting the quote, direct the customer to raise_request or a branch visit to proceed with foreclosure.

as_of_date.description: Value date for the quote. Defaults to the current server date; a future date may be passed to plan ahead.

function.name: calculate_emi
function.description:
Computes the fixed monthly EMI, total interest, total repayment, and full amortisation schedule for a loan.

Category: calculators | Action type: calculator

Call before this tool, in order:
?. get_deposit_loan_rates — rate should be sourced here for actual loan bookings; a customer-supplied rate is permitted only for hypothetical/exploratory 'what-if' calculations, not for use in an actual transaction.

Notes:
- Interest and principal split changes every month even though the emi total is fixed — early installments are interest-heavy, later ones principal-heavy, because interest is charged on the shrinking outstanding balance.
- closing_balance at the last installment should be 0.

function.name: get_gold_rate
function.description:
Returns today's gold rate per gram for a given purity. Sole valid source for gold_rate_per_gram in calculate_gold_loan_ltv — never assume, recall, or accept this value from customer input.

Category: loans | Action type: read

Related tools: calculate_gold_loan_ltv

purity_karat.description: Must match the purity of the gold being pledged.

function.name: calculate_gold_loan_ltv
function.description:
Values gold collateral (grams x rate) and applies the bank's current Loan-to-Value cap to compute the maximum eligible loan amount. The LTV cap itself is applied internally by the backend, not supplied by the caller.

Category: calculators | Action type: calculator

Call before this tool, in order:
1. get_gold_rate — gold_rate_per_gram must come from a fresh call at the same purity — never assumed or customer-supplied

Related tools: get_gold_rate

Notes:
- Always pass the rate_per_gram returned by get_gold_rate for the same purity_karat — this links the calculation to a verifiable rate source, which is why the rate must be supplied by the caller rather than fetched internally.

purity_karat.description: Must match the purity used in the get_gold_rate call.

gold_rate_per_gram.description: Rate from get_gold_rate for the same purity.

function.name: get_card_details
function.description:
Returns card metadata, status, credit/available limits, and per-channel usage controls. Use to diagnose card declines.

Category: cards | Action type: read

Related tools: set_card_controls, toggle_card_freeze, block_card

Notes:
- Mandatory prerequisite before set_card_controls — surface current settings before proposing changes.

function.name: toggle_card_freeze
function.description:
Temporarily freezes or unfreezes a card. Reversible at any time. Use freeze when a card is misplaced but may be found.
For loss, theft, fraud, or damage use block_card instead, which is permanent.

Category: cards | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Call  get_card_details before this tool

Notes:
- Cannot unfreeze a card whose status is blocked or expired — only active/frozen cards are valid targets.

function.name: block_card
function.description:
Permanently and irreversibly blocks a card. Confirm the customer understands this before calling. For fraud, theft, or loss, block immediately. For damaged cards, block to enable a replacement request. A replacement can be requested via raise_request.

Category: cards | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling and also ask for a reason to block the card

Call get_card_details before this tool

function.name: set_card_controls
function.description:
Updates per-channel card controls. Each channel (atm, online, pos) has independent domestic and international enable/limit settings. Only provided fields change; omitted fields keep their current values.

Category: cards | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Call before this tool, in order:
1. get_card_details — provide current control settings before proposing changes

Notes:
- For enabling/disabling the channel. Only call the tool if the current and requested status is different.
- For changing limits, follow:
-- Check if the channel is enabled. 
-- The requested limit must be less than the credit_limit.
-- The requested limit should not be equal to the current limit
-- The requested limit should not be negative

- For requests containing multiple parameters in a channel/channels:
-- Send the same control dictionary with the requested changes.

- Do not make changes to a channel's enable/disable status and daily limit in the same tool call.
- If required do sequential tool calls to fulfill the user's request.
- The channel objects (atm / online / pos) are optional in the schema but they carry the request: omitting all of them changes nothing. If the customer has not made clear which channel, which region (domestic/international), or what value they want, ask — never guess a channel or invent a limit to avoid asking.

atm.description: ATM cash withdrawal controls. Omit to leave unchanged.

online.description: Online (card-not-present) payment controls. Omit to leave unchanged.

pos.description: In-store POS transaction controls. Omit to leave unchanged.

function.name: show_mandates
function.description:
Lists mandates on the customer's profile. Recurring subscription debits are mandates, not card transactions — look them up here, not via card tools.

Category: mandates | Action type: read

Notes:If a customer asks about a mandate or wants it cancelled, paused or resumed, inform them of this limitation and direct them to raise_request or a branch visit.

account_id.description: Filter to mandates on one linked account. All accounts if omitted.

function.name: stop_cheque_payment
function.description:
Places a stop-payment instruction on one or more cheques issued from an account. Only affects cheques that have not already cleared; per-cheque outcomes are returned individually.

Category: cheques | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Notes:
- Cheque clearing status is checked in the backend at call time, not supplied by the caller — a cheque that has already cleared is returned with a failed per-cheque outcome rather than being blocked pre-emptively by the model.

account_id.description: Linked account the cheques were issued from.

function.name: request_cheque_book
function.description:
Orders a new cheque book for a savings or current account.

Category: service_requests | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

function.name: request_duplicate_statement
function.description:
Orders an official duplicate account statement for a date range, delivered by email. Use this — not raw get_transaction_history output

Category: service_requests | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Related tools: get_transaction_history, get_request_status

Notes:
- The statement does not include the per-entry status field returned by get_transaction_history — it lists only cleared/posted transactions.

function.name: raise_request
function.description:
Registers a complaint or general service request — the single escalation channel for disputes, service issues, and any action no other tool can perform (e.g. card replacement after block_card, insurance premium/claim needs, premature-closure follow-up beyond close_deposit, postal address update).

Category: service_requests | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Call before this tool, in order:
1. get_transaction_history — locate the disputed transaction and pass its reference_id as related_transaction_id

Related tools: get_transaction_history, get_request_status, get_all_requests, block_card

Notes:
- unauthorized_debit requests are treated as urgent by default.
- Never promise a specific outcome, e.g. a fee waiver — the request is routed for review, not resolved on the spot.
- related_transaction_id is required when category is failed_transaction or unauthorized_debit — this is not enforced at the schema level and must be validated at call time.
- This system has no tool to update a customer's email, phone number, or postal address. Direct customers requesting any of these to raise_request.
- category has no default and must always be explicitly chosen — pick the closest fit rather than a catch-all; there is no general_query option.

description.description: What happened / what is needed, with enough context to action it.

related_transaction_id.description: reference_id of the disputed transaction from get_transaction_history. Required for failed_transaction and unauthorized_debit.

account_id.description: Related linked account, if applicable — helps routing.

function.name: get_request_status
function.description:
Returns the current status of a previously raised service request. Use when a customer follows up on an earlier request, before raising a duplicate.

Category: service_requests | Action type: read

Related tools: get_all_requests

request_id.description: Service request ID returned by any request tool.

function.name: get_all_requests
function.description:
Lists the customer's service requests (raised via raise_request, request_cheque_book, request_duplicate_statement, or stop_cheque_payment), most recent first. Use when a customer asks about their outstanding or past requests generally, without a specific request_id — use get_request_status instead once a specific request_id is known.

Category: service_requests | Action type: read

Related tools: get_request_status, raise_request

category.description: Filter by request category. All categories if omitted.

function.name: get_insurance_details
function.description:
Returns policy details for the customer's bancassurance policies. No premium-payment or claim tools exist in this system — route those needs via raise_request.

Category: insurance | Action type: read

Related tools: raise_request

function.name: get_products_and_offers
function.description:
Returns a combined list of the bank's products and the customer's personalised offers, optionally filtered by type. You represent the bank, not an independent advisor — proactively call this and recommend relevant products/offers whenever a natural opening appears in the conversation (e.g. after closing a deposit, suggest reinvestment options; after discussing a loan or card, mention relevant pre-approved offers), not only when the customer explicitly asks 'what do you offer'.

Category: catalog | Action type: read

Related tools: get_deposit_loan_rates

Notes:
- You act on behalf of the bank commercially — default toward recommending the bank's own products/offers over generic advice, and look for a relevant moment to surface one in most conversations, even ones that didn't start as a product inquiry.
- Being bank-favouring does not mean being inaccurate: never state an offer is guaranteed or already approved, never overstate benefits, and never quote interest rates from this catalog — always use get_deposit_loan_rates as the authoritative source.
